heading: ## The leg ledger — replay, receipt, and how it is read (round 7, measured)
notes: The section's first paragraph is a dated round-7 record and every load-bearing claim in it re-verified true at C0. The r7-1 runner is the revision the section names: `git show 9f1d3c3:tools/mutate-and-run.sh` hashes to cf41efaa8be5f52d92bf7806ddb3a99a031547bf12a6811b8ef45bce37242c75, i.e. 61 632 B / 1 341 L — exactly the 'cf41efaa… (r7-1; 1 341 L / 61 632 B)' pin the ledger's ER-2 names (corpus/knowledge/fleet-kill-rate-ledger.md:281). So the section's `tools/mutate-and-run.sh@9f1d3c3` anchor and the ledger's r7-1 blob pin are the same artifact, not two names for one thing.

The four legs and their recorded kill-rates are quoted verbatim from the r7-1 header the section cites: at 9f1d3c3 lines 75-78 name js-kimi-census (r2, 8/10 = 80 %), bash-surface-census (r3, 8/10 = 80 %), bash-tsukuroi-census (r5, 6/10 = 60 %), bash-mado-verify (r6, 4/10 = 40 %), and the section's list matches line for line and rate for rate. The same four rates appear as ledger rows 1-4 (corpus/knowledge/fleet-kill-rate-ledger.md:45-48) with the same r2/r3/r5/r6 round labels, so the section's parenthetical revision labels are the ledger's own, not a re-derivation.

The section's second anchor, `:511-522` at 9f1d3c3, resolves to the pin/revision/table block for exactly those four legs (PIN_JS..REV_MADO on 511-518, TABLE_JS..TABLE_MADO on 519-522) — 12 lines, no fifth leg. `git show 9f1d3c3:tools/mutate-and-run.sh | grep -cE '^  regression_case_git (js|bash)-'` returns 4, so 'four legs at r7-1' is the whole leg set at that revision, not a subset. The pre-r7-1 runner (44947154) had 0 such legs and its `--regression` was the r4-2 two-case self-check the section says round 7 replaced ('re-runs BOTH worked cases', 'cases=2' in its summary printfs), so the section's framing of round 7 as the turn from two-case self-check to the fleet ledger is accurate.

The round-18 pointer resolves to a genuine round-18 revision: 4b7c682 is the commit 'round-18: measured SCORECARD depth7→8, bounded eleven-defect closure, strict60/60 calibration8' and its runner blob hashes to d22c4025e8ce38b8890bedc1eb9eb5f61366c22f4741910bbe5a942582294a8b — the same sha the round-18 receipt carries on its REGRESSION_TOOL line (.ufo/waves/round-18/w2/RerunC1.md:84). Note the section names a commit rev where the ledger and the receipt name a blob sha256; the two agree because that commit is the one carrying that blob.

The milestone list in the section ('seven from round 16, eight from round 18, nine from round 26, ten from round 51') was checked against the committed receipts of those four rounds and each is exact: `REGRESSION: PASS (cases=7 passed=7; …)` (.ufo/evidence/round-16/round-gate/runner-regression.txt:41), `(cases=8 passed=8; …)` (.ufo/evidence/round-18/coldread/traces/CR18/2.out.txt:45), `(cases=9 passed=9; …)` (.ufo/evidence/round-26/cite-check/regression-worktree.stdout:50) and `(cases=10 passed=10; …)` (.ufo/evidence/round-51/integrate/l1-probe-f133b47/c2.stdout:22). The enumeration does not list the intermediate 5-and-6 milestone (the two legs embedded at r10-2), but each listed item is true and the same enumeration is used in the sibling sections at SKILL.md:980 and :1006 and in the registry row at :1426, so it reads as a house convention rather than a gap in this heading.

The row arithmetic in the section's closing parenthetical holds. The ledger's rate table carries rows 1-4 in §1 (lines 45-48) and rows 5-6 in the ER-2 append table (lines 276-277) — six in the §1/ER-2 table — plus one appended row each in the 'Round 16 — seventh row appended' (line 403, js-round-gate) and 'Round 18 — eighth row appended' (line 424, js-sources-check) blocks: eight ledger rows in total, matching the registry row at SKILL.md:1426 ('eight rows').

The claim that the ninth and tenth cases are 'recorded in their own notes, not as ledger rows' is literally true and slightly understates the tenth's footprint. Both notes exist at C0 — corpus/knowledge/mutation-case-kumitate-cite-check.md (ninth, '## 2. The ninth case has no ledger footprint at all (the ledger contains no round-26 cite-check block); the tenth does have one, as the 'Round 52 — §3 drift-pins cell superseded' block at line 439, which records the case-10 measurement and the note pointer. That block is a cell supersession, not a rate row, so the section's sentence stands as written; SKILL.md:1426 already states the tenth's only ledger footprint precisely.
